Author: Aravind Kumar
Bench: Aravind Kumar
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No. Of 2025
 @ Special Leave Petition (Criminal)
 No.16676/2025
 Vinod Appellant
 Versus
 State Of Madhya Pradesh Respondent
 O R D E R
1.
Heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties.

2. Leave granted.
3. Appellant was tried for an offence punishable under Section 376(3) of the Indian Penal Code,
1860 and Sections 5(L)/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (the POCSO Act) came to be convicted and 1 Crl.No.___ of 2025 @ SLP (Crl.) No.16676/2025 imprisonment for each of the offence which was ordered to run concurrently alongwith the fine and default sentences.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The same has been challenged and same is pending in Criminal Appeal No.1118/2022 before the jurisdictional High Court.

On the premise that the age of the prosecutrix was 14 years 01 month; and the DNA found was held to be positive; and also on the ground that appellant had treated her cruelly, the discretionary relief of bail by suspending the sentence was denied.
Hence, this appeal.

4. Learned counsel appearing for the respondent  State has vehemently contended that presumption which would arise under Sections 29 and 30 of the POCSO Act in the facts of the present case has not been rebutted and as such he has prayed for dismissal of the appeal.
5. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties and on perusal of the case records, it would disclose that learned trial Judge while recording the testimony of the 2 Crl.No.___ of 2025 @
Vinod vs State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190191364/
1 SLP (Crl.) No.16676/2025 prosecutrix has made a note that the age of the prosecutrix is 14 to 16 years; that apart the prosecutrix herself has admitted in the cross- examination that there were many villages on the way from Ghonsla to Pune while she travelled with the appellant.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the issues relating to illegal confinement or the appellant having meted out cruelty on the prosecutrix are debatable and require to be examined by the appellate court after re-appreciation of the evidence.
However, we do not propose to express any views in that regard, as it is likely to prejudice the case of either parties.
The observations made hereinabove is to the limited extent of examining the prayer for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.
It also requires to be noticed that the appeal is of the year 2022 and the chances of same being taken up for final disposal in the near future is very remote.
For this reason also, we are of the considered view that appellant would be entitled for the relief(s) sought for.
Hence, the appeal 3 Crl.No.___ of 2025 @ SLP (Crl.) No.16676/2025 is allowed.
The sentence imposed on the appellant shall stand suspended and appellant is ordered to be released on bail on such terms and conditions as deem fit by the jurisdictional Sessions Court.
The appeal stands allowed.
6. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

.................J. (ARAVIND KUMAR) .................J. (N.V. ANJARIA) NEW DELHI;
DECEMBER 04, 2025.
